openings.claim: Pencil each envelope with its assigned pattern and sample-derived material-tag/count pairs; tick quantities only after insertion. This explicitly binds sample requirements, tray identification and actual transfer, potentially detecting omissions during filling and making assignment visible at distribution. Shared-material omissions and rare sample consultation motivate the hypothesis; neither identifies the omission stage.
openings.discriminator: Compare the bound ledger with tags alone, samples alone and unlinked parents to test binding-specific benefit. Separately compare matched loose local staging without quantity cues: reduced crossings, time and omissions there would favour spatial interference. Correctly ticked incomplete envelopes defeat insertion checking; no advantage over unlinked parents defeats the interaction claim. O4 challenges shared-tray necessity but has unknown pattern mixture.
openings.probe: Z1 proposes three matched four-kit batches within 18 minutes including preparation/audit: incumbent, ledger with shared trays, and uncued local staging. A1 proposes counterbalanced matched blocks comparing baseline, each parent, unlinked parents and hybrid within 90 minutes. These answer distinct questions. Record setup, assembly, checking, corrections, omissions, crossings and footprint; audit against samples. Stop staging if it exceeds the table. Screening cannot establish full-run hybrid performance.
openings.uncertainty: Quantity-memory dominance, picking versus filling errors, sample readability, legible envelope space, matched assignments, staging and opened-packet footprints, probe feasibility and 60-kit completion remain unknown. Distribution benefit is also untested; all observations are synthetic stipulations.

lineage.reason: Retains insertion ticks, exterior assignment, spatial rival and bounded comparison.
Retains explicit sample/tag/count/transfer binding and component-interaction comparison.

decision: Screen before adoption. Preserve specified quantities/dimensions, exactly two volunteers for at most 90 minutes, the existing 180-by-75-centimetre table and existing envelopes/supplies without purchases or new equipment. Success requires all 60 complete assigned kits before the workshop, at most one distribution correction. Neither source establishes this or addresses hidden reserve-stock replenishment.
